requirements.text: The block works for every `N` from 2 to 32, and bits `N` and up of the `ENABLE`, `MODE` and `PENDING` registers read as zero and ignore writes.
While `rst_n` is low at a rising edge of `clk`, `ENABLE`, `MODE` and `PENDING` clear to zero and the remembered level of every source clears to zero.
A write to `ENABLE` or `MODE` stores `wdata` bits `N-1` to 0 in that register.
A read never changes any register; `rdata` follows `addr` with no clock edge.
A high-level source sets its `PENDING` bit at every rising edge where its input is high.
A rising-edge source sets its `PENDING` bit at a rising edge where its input is high and was low at the previous rising edge, so an input held high sets it once.
Detection does not depend on `ENABLE`: a disabled source still sets its `PENDING` bit.
A write to `PENDING` clears each bit written 1 and leaves each bit written 0 unchanged; it never sets a bit.
A write to `CLAIM` acknowledges the source whose number is in `wdata` bits 4 to 0: that source's `PENDING` bit clears and no other bit changes; a number of `N` or more changes nothing.
A source detected at the same rising edge as a write that clears its bit keeps its `PENDING` bit set, so a high-level source acknowledged while its input is still high stays pending.
`irq` is high exactly when some source has both its `PENDING` and its `ENABLE` bit set, for high-level and rising-edge sources alike.
`irq_id` is the lowest-numbered source whose `PENDING` and `ENABLE` bits are both set, so source 0 has the highest priority, and it is 0 while `irq` is low.
A read of `CLAIM` returns `irq` in bit 31 and `irq_id` in bits 4 to 0, with every other bit zero.
`irq` and `irq_id` follow the registers with no clock edge, so a source detected at one rising edge drives `irq` until the next.

items.name: Reset values and reset from a busy state
items.rationale: Both lanes read every register and the claim after the first reset and again after a reset with every source pending.

items.name: ENABLE and MODE write and read back
items.rationale: Patterns and all ones are written and read back at N 8 and N 5; bits N and up must read zero.

items.name: Reads change nothing
items.rationale: CLAIM and PENDING are read repeatedly between edges and must not move; every read is sampled with no clock edge.

items.name: High-level detection
items.rationale: A held level must stay pending through a PENDING clear and an acknowledge, and clear only once low.

items.name: Rising-edge detection
items.rationale: An input held high fires once; a falling edge fires nothing; a second rising edge fires again.

items.name: Detection and masking while disabled
items.rationale: A disabled source of each mode must set PENDING while irq, irq_id and CLAIM stay quiet; enabling it raises irq.

items.name: Write-1-to-clear
items.rationale: With every source pending, one bit written 1 clears that bit alone; a write of zero clears nothing; a write of ones to an empty PENDING sets nothing.

items.name: Acknowledge
items.rationale: Each in-range number clears only its bit; every number from N to 31 is written and must change nothing; bits above 4 are ignored.

items.name: Detection at the edge of its clear
items.rationale: A rising edge lands at the very edge of a PENDING clear and of an acknowledge; the bit must stay set.

items.name: Fixed priority and the claim
items.rationale: With several sources pending, irq_id and the CLAIM read must name the lowest enabled one, skip disabled ones, and walk up in order as each is acknowledged.

items.name: Outputs with no added cycle
items.rationale: irq and irq_id are checked 1 ns after the edge that detects or clears, with no extra edge.
